 Deion Sanders after Colorado’s blowout loss to Oklahoma State: “I really don’t understand it”
 By
 Mike Florio , 
 By
 Mike Florio 
     Published October 25, 2026 07:46 AM 
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email
 Deion Sanders’s fourth season as head coach of the Colorado Buffaloes started with an upset of Georgia Tech and a blowout of overmatched Weber State.
 Since then, the wheels have come off.
 The Buffs have lost five in a row, capped by a 57-24 blowout loss to Oklahoma State on Saturday. Colorado actually led the game at halftime, 24-23. In the second half, the Cowboys outscored the Buffaloes, 34-0.
 “We’re so disciplined in this and that, and this and that, and every darn thing we do, but it seems like as soon as we go in the field, we’re not disciplined,” Sanders said after the game, via Brent Schrotenboer of USA Today . “I really don’t understand it, because we are disciplined in every area of this program, when it comes to academics, when it comes to being somewhere on time, when it comes to wearing the proper uniform, when it comes to just your manners in the building. Everything. But [when] we get on the field at the most critical moments, we blow it .”
 The latest loss may have sparked another quarterback change, after Kaneal Sweetwyne replaced Isaac Wilson, who had replaced Julian Lewis in September.
 The end result is that Colorado hasn’t won a Big 12 road game since 2024. And the Buffaloes are 2-15 against Power Four conferences since December 2024.
